findings.body:
**Anchor vendor findings to the revision whose lines the vendor reported.**

`completionEvent` reads each finding's blob from the target tree (`src/policy/crq/backfillCompletion.ts:261`) and keeps the vendor's raw line numbers. The vendor reviews the head revision. The submitted scope already uses head blobs (`backfillCompletion.ts:59-71`), so a finding's line numbers and its blob can come from different revisions. When the target blob for a finding's path differs from the head blob, the finding can carry `anchor_status: "verified"` while pointing at lines in different content.

The ledger validation accepts this. It requires only a path, a blob, and non-empty intervals for a verified finding (`src/policy/crq/ledger.ts:704-717`). Neither verifier compares a finding's blob or intervals with head. Both verifiers enforce target-equals-head blobs only for `reviewed_scope` entries (`src/adapters/crq/backfillAccounting.ts:704-716`, `src/adapters/crq/reviewVerify.ts:254-265`). Findings on paths outside the credited scope are not covered.

Choose one anchor revision for findings. Either resolve the finding blob from the head entries and reject a finding whose anchor cannot be matched to head, or validate the finding blob against head and its intervals against the head-side changed lines. Then keep the target tree only for the intended target-side use. The repository does not establish which revision findings must anchor to, so this comment gives no code patch.
findings.title: Anchor vendor findings to the revision whose lines the vendor reported.

findings.body:
**Stop a receiptless finding row from writing a second outcome on replay.**

When `planRepairHarvest` writes a row, the returned row keeps the input's receipt state. If the input row has no `receipt`, the returned row has none either, and it is persisted for later reads. If the same job later harvests that persisted row, the receipt guard passes. `priorRetriableOutcomes` then counts the first `crq-repair` event, so a `needs-retriage` outcome becomes `needs-human` once the count reaches `maxFindingRetries`. The changed action changes `sourceKey`, so the `already-recorded` check misses and a second `finding-event` is written. One attempt therefore records two outcomes and uses up the retry allowance early.

Rows that carry the job's receipt are protected. The status check rejects them because the first write sets `status` to the action, which is not `delivered`.

This path needs a later harvest of the persisted receiptless row for the same job. The inspected code does not show whether the queue can redeliver a completed item or whether the receipt is always written before harvest. Confirm that one of these cannot occur, or bind the replay to the job before writing. Otherwise, refuse a receiptless row that already has a finding-event predecessor.
findings.title: Stop a receiptless finding row from writing a second outcome on replay.
